newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - July 9.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The retail issue price of ICI Australia Ltd shares is expected to finalise at the top end of the offer price range. Strong demand has seen predictions of a A$12.40 per share price confirmed when ICIA's share price fell yesterday A$12.80, however institutions are yet to be fully convinced over the value of the ICIA sell-down. Page 19.

Talks on the rationalisation of the pay-TV industry between major players News Corporation and Telstra's Foxtel have produced a tentative agreement whereby both companies would participate in a A$700 million listing through the floundering Australis Media Ltd. The move comes after the Federal Government and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission recently signalled they would not oppose any rationalisation in pay-TV if it will benefit consumers. Page 19. --

The West Australian Government yesterday indicated some flexibility on the imposition of its proposed gold royalty. Resources Development Minister Colin Barnett said that while a 1.25 per cent royalty on production would proceed next year, any increase in the levy would be linked to the gold price. Page 20. --

The Australian Bureau of Statistics said yesterday that the upcoming balance of payments figures would include the Reserve Bank's recent sale of gold reserves, which was equal to about half the total value of gold exports in 1996. The inclusion will mean that Australia's export income will be boosted by approximately A$2.4 billion this year. Page 20.

Austrim Ltd yesterday acquired over 1 million shares, or 3 per cent, of their take-over target Hawker Richardson. The extra shares have boosted Austrim's holdings in Hawker to 26.3 per cent and ensured its effective control of the company. Page 21.

BHP Co Ltd is investigating the possibility of taking a major international partner into its integrated manganese business in order to capitalise on expected expansions in the Asian steel market. Likely contenders include major Japanese steel-makers, and existing ferro-alloy manufacturers who are already supplying the steel industry. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Plans by insurance giant AMP Society to launch its long awaited demutualisation and float later this year are expected to be delayed by legal challenges from dissatisfied policy holders. Analysts agree the Australian Mutual Provident Society (Demutualisation and Reconstruction) Act, recently passed by the New South Wales Parliament, is vulnerable to legal attack on a number of points. Page 21.

The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) has launched an a exhaustive probe into securities lending following the clampdown on franking credits announced in the Federal Budget. The ATO is focusing its investigation on transactions completed by Australian Stock Exchange broker members on the CHESS settlements system from July 1995 to May 7 1997, one week before the last Federal Budget. Page 21.

Industrial battery group Kinetic Power plans to raise A$16 million through a public offering of 16 million A$1 dollar shares. The extra funds are required for the company to build an export battery plant in Brisbane. Page 22.

Century Zinc managing director Ian Williams confirmed yesterday that the company will begin construction of its A$1.1 billion Gulf of Carpentaria mine by October, and it has already received enthusiastic employment enquiries from local Aborigines. Williams said work on obtaining clearances for the mine site was progressing steadily. Page 22.

Following deregulation Telstra is attempting to retain its share of the A$1 billion a year data market by pushing its data services in a renewed marketing drive that will emphasise consumers over products. The telecommunications industry will undergo major changes in the near future when data traffic exceeds voice traffic, and data becomes the prime factor in business revenue and profits. Page 23.

Mining company North managing director Campbell Anderson confirmed yesterday that the A$220 million Lake Cowal gold project in New South Wales has been stalled due to the current gold prices. Anderson said production wouldn't be viable with gold currently priced at just above US$300 an ounce. Page 24.

News Corp is believed to be moving to quit its 40 percent stake in publisher and multimedia group PMP Communications, with broker JB Were sounding out potential investors on behalf of the media giant.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

News Corp is selling its 40 per cent stake in PMP Communications as part of a move to leave the Australian magazine industry. Over 100 million shares are being sold by stockbroker JB Were for A$325 million, but the lack of formal announcement by News Corp has sparked speculation that Weres struggled to find institutional interest. Page 29.

Property Investment Research has released a report on Australia's most powerful property owners, titled Australian Landlord, revealing 50 landlords hold up to 70 per cent of all commercial property. AMP Society has topped the list, holding A$6 billion worth of shopping centres, warehouses and office blocks. Page 29.

A reduction in official interest rates is looking unlikely after the Australian dollar yesterday fell to US74.25 cents, its lowest level since January 1996. However, Prime Minister John Howard has increased pressure on the Reserve Bank, saying that he would like to see rates fall again. Page 29.

Stockmarket analysts believe Brambles Industries has paid between A$70 million and A$100 million for Chep New Zealand, in a deal yet to be approved by the New Zealand Overseas Investment Commission. Rival GE Capital Services was outbid on the deal, but has recently purchased Loscum, Bramble's major competitor for the Australian pallet market. Page 31.

Transport group Holyman filed a prospectus yesterday in a bid to raise A$49.1 million to purchase Union Shipping Group's Australian shipping operations from Brierley Investments. The proposed deal is subject to shareholder approval, with the purchase expected to cost A$58.3 million. Page 33.

AMP superannuation general manager Steve Trotter believes changes to superannuation policy introduced by the Howard Government will mean that everyone must save more to provide for their retirement. Trotter says there is now a greater emphasis on voluntary savings and choice of funds rather than compulsory savings. Page 31.
THE AGE

Share price losses in the gold sector have risen to more than A$2 billion after a third day of meltdown in stocks yesterday. The Gold Index closed 82 points down on morning trade to close at 1193 points, with analysts predicting over 20 gold operations will close if conditions do not improve quickly. Page B1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has called for an inquiry by the Industry Commission into Australia's black coal industry. Resources and Energy Minister Warwick Parer said the inquiry would provide benchmarks for the industry and identify ways of improvng its international competitiveness. Page B3.

The value of gold equities held by Australian superannuation funds has fallen by about A$1 billion in the past week in the face of panic selling by small investors in the stockmarket. Market analysts believe the rush has forced share prices down irrationally and large lines of gold stocks are without buyers. Page B1.

As part of a strategy by News Corp to raise A$1 billion through the sale of non-core assets, the industry giant is selling its 40 per cent stake in PMP Communications for A$325 million. PMP is valued at A$800 million and market analysts believe the sale f the shares to be a difficult task due to PMP's recent decline in earnings. Page B1.

The ICI Australia share offer will be oversubscribed when it closes today, with brokers claiming there has been a very strong retail response. The demand has been helped by an increase in the company's stocks, which have traded above the selling price. Page B3.

Richard Pratt's Visy Industries and Brierley Investments are contenders for the management rights to Cairns' Reef casino-hotel complex. The casino is currently operated by Sinophil Corp, with a lease to operate the venture available for A$11.5 million. Pge B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
